# Create Data Set for Analysis

```{r data-setup}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false


if (file.exists(here::here("Data/data-analysis-nested.csv"))) {
  
  # Load data files for analysis if they're already created.
  data.analysis <- read_csv(here::here("Data/data-analysis.csv"))

  data.analysis.nested <- read_csv(here::here("Data/data-analysis-nested.csv"))
  
  
} else {


# Clean exports to US IMF data
exports.to.us <- readr::read_csv(here::here("Data/Raw Data/imf-dots/Imports_from_Counterpart_Countries.csv")) |> 
  dplyr::rename("country" = "COUNTERPART_COUNTRY") |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(country)) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(ccode = countrycode::countrycode(country, origin = "country.name",  destination = "cown"),
                region = countrycode(ccode, origin = "cown", destination = "region")) |> 
  dplyr::rename("year" = "TIME_PERIOD", "exports_to_us" = "OBS_VALUE") |> 
  dplyr::select(country, ccode, region, year, exports_to_us) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(country) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(exports_to_us = as.numeric(exports_to_us)) |> 
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2000)


# Clean imports from US IMF data
imports.from.us <- readr::read_csv(here::here("Data/Raw Data/imf-dots/Exports_to_Counterpart_Countries.csv")) |> 
  dplyr::rename("country" = "COUNTERPART_COUNTRY") |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(country)) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(ccode = countrycode::countrycode(country, origin = "country.name",  destination = "cown"),
                region = countrycode(ccode, origin = "cown", destination = "region")) |> 
  dplyr::rename("year" = "TIME_PERIOD", "imports_from_us" = "OBS_VALUE") |> 
  dplyr::select(country, ccode, region, year, imports_from_us) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(country) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(imports_from_us = as.numeric(imports_from_us)) |> 
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2000)


options(digits = 3)
# Health Data from World Bank WDI
health.data <- readxl::read_xlsx(here::here("Data/Raw Data/P_Data_Extract_From_Health_Nutrition_and_Population_Statistics/P_Data_Extract_From_World_Development_Indicators.xlsx")) |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(`Series Code`)) |> 
  dplyr::rename("variable" = 1, "country" = 3) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(5:29)) |> 
  group_by(country) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(name = as.numeric(str_extract(name, "\\d{4} ")),
                value = case_when(
                  grepl("\\.\\.", value) ~ NA,
                  TRUE ~ round(as.numeric(value), 3)
                )) |> 
  dplyr::rename("year" = "name") |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(ccode = countrycode(variable,
                                    origin = "country.name",
                                    destination = "cown")) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("variable", "ccode", "year"),
              names_from = "country",
              values_from = "value") |>
  dplyr::rename("country" = "variable",
                "infant_deaths_num" = `Number of infant deaths`,
                "infant_mortality" = `Mortality rate, infant (per 1,000 live births)`,
                "infant_mortality_female" = `Mortality rate, infant, female (per 1,000 live births)`,
                "infant_mortality_male" = `Mortality rate, infant, male (per 1,000 live births)`,
                "hospital_beds_per_1000" = `Hospital beds (per 1,000 people)`,
                "healthcare_expenditures_pc" = `Current health expenditure per capita (current US$)`,
                "healthcare_expenditures" = `Current health expenditure (% of GDP)`,
                "healthcare_expenditures_gov" = `Domestic general government health expenditure (% of GDP)`,
                "healthcare_expenditures_gov_pc" = `Domestic general government health expenditure (% of current health expenditure)`,
                "material_mortality_ratio_modeled" = `Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)`,
                "material_mortality_ratio" = `Maternal mortality ratio (national estimate, per 100,000 live births)`,
                "population_growth" = `Population growth (annual %)`,
                "unemployment_rate" = `Unemployment, total (% of total labor force) (national estimate)`,
                "trade_gdp" = `Trade (% of GDP)`,
                "gdp_constant" = `GDP (constant 2015 US$)`,
                ) |> 
  dplyr::select(ccode, year, everything()) |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ccode))


# Health Data Addendum
health.data.2 <- read_csv(here::here("Data/Raw Data/P_Data_Extract_From_Health_Nutrition_and_Population_Statistics/8efd2565-8927-4877-a42a-9c6ebee02db2_Data.csv")) |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(`Series Code`)) |> 
  dplyr::rename("variable" = 1, "country" = 3) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(5:29)) |> 
  group_by(country) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(name = as.numeric(str_extract(name, "\\d{4} ")),
                value = case_when(
                  grepl("\\.\\.", value) ~ NA,
                  TRUE ~ round(as.numeric(value), 3)
                )) |> 
  dplyr::rename("year" = "name") |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(ccode = countrycode(country,
                                    origin = "country.name",
                                    destination = "cown")) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("country", "ccode", "year"),
              names_from = "variable",
              values_from = "value") |> 
  dplyr::rename("hospital_beds" = `Hospital beds (per 1,000 people)`,
                "infant_mortality_rate" = `Mortality rate, infant (per 1,000 live births)`,
                "infant_mortality_rate_female" = `Mortality rate, infant, female (per 1,000 live births)`,
                "infant_mortality_rate_male" = `Mortality rate, infant, male (per 1,000 live births)`,
                "infant_deaths_num" = `Number of infant deaths`,
                "population_total" = `Population, total`,
                "education_spending" = `Public spending on education, total (% of GDP)`,
                "population_rural" = `Rural population (% of total population)`,
                "population_urban" = `Urban population (% of total population)`
  )
  


# Homicide Data
# Rate per 100,000 people. Both sexes.
homicide.data <- readr::read_csv(here::here("Data/WHO/homicide-data.csv")) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(ccode = countrycode::countrycode(Location, origin = "country.name", destination = "cown"),
                homicide_rate = FactValueNumeric,
                year = Period) |> 
  dplyr::filter(Dim1 == "Both sexes") |> 
  dplyr::select(ccode, year, homicide_rate)

# Iraq Contributions
iraq.contributions <- readxl::read_xlsx(here::here("Data/Raw Data/Iraq Coalition Contributions.xlsx")) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(ccode = countrycode::countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "cown")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(iraq_coalition = 1,
                beginyear = as.Date(beginyear),
                endyear = as.Date(endyear)) |> 
  rowwise() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(time = list(lubridate::year(beginyear):lubridate::year(endyear))) |> 
  tidyr::unnest(time) |> 
  dplyr::select(country, ccode, time, iraq_coalition, dead, wounded, troopstotal, troopspeak) |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(c(dead, wounded, troopstotal, troopspeak),
                       ~ as.numeric(.x))) |> 
  dplyr::rename("year" = "time")

# Create ccode list for more general Iraq coalition of the willing dummy variable.
iraq.ccode.list <- unique(iraq.contributions$ccode)

# V-Dem Data
vdem.data <- vdemdata::vdem  |> 
  dplyr::filter(year >= 1999) |> 
  dplyr::select(country_name, COWcode, year, v2x_polyarchy, v2x_libdem) |> 
  dplyr::rename("ccode" = COWcode, "country" = country_name)


#  UN Voting data
un.data <- read_csv(here::here("Data/Raw Data/IdealpointestimatesAll_Jun2024.csv")) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(year = session + 1945) |> 
  dplyr::filter(year>=1999) |>
  group_by(year) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(US_Idealpoint = IdealPointAll[ccode==2],
                un_distance_abs = abs(US_Idealpoint - IdealPointAll),
                un_distance = US_Idealpoint - IdealPointAll) |> 
  dplyr::select(year, ccode, USAgree, un_distance) 


# BTH/NH Deployment Indicator
deployment.indicator <- readxl::read_xlsx(here::here("Data/SOUTHCOM Data/BTH History.xlsx")) |> 
  group_by(Country, Year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(deployment = 1) |>
  ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(ccode = countrycode::countrycode(sourcevar = Country, 
                                                 origin = "country.name", 
                                                 destination = "cown")) |> 
  dplyr::rename("year" = "Year")

# Homicide Data


# Centroid data for country capitals
centroid.df <- CoordinateCleaner::countryref |> 
  dplyr::mutate(ccode = countrycode::countrycode(sourcevar = iso3, 
                                                  origin = "iso3c", 
                                                  destination = "cown")) |> 
  dplyr::filter(type == "country") |> 
  dplyr::group_by(ccode) |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ccode)) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(ccode = first(ccode),
                   capital.lon = first(capital.lon), 
                   capital.lat = first(capital.lat)) 


data.analysis <- peacesciencer::create_stateyears(system = "cow", subset_years = c(1998:2024)) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(region = countrycode::countrycode(sourcevar = ccode, 
                                                  origin = "cown", 
                                                  destination = "region")) |> 
  dplyr::filter(region == "Latin America & Caribbean") |> 
  left_join(health.data, by = c("ccode", "year")) |>
  left_join(health.data.2, by = c("ccode", "year")) |> 
  left_join(vdem.data, by = c("ccode", "year")) |> 
  left_join(exports.to.us, by = c("ccode", "year")) |>
  left_join(imports.from.us, by = c("ccode", "year")) |>
  left_join(un.data, by = c("ccode", "year")) |>
  left_join(deployment.indicator, by = c("ccode", "year")) |> 
  left_join(iraq.contributions, by = c("ccode", "year")) |>
  left_join(homicide.data, by = c("ccode", "year")) |> 
  left_join(centroid.df, by = "ccode") |>
  mutate(deployment = case_when(
    is.na(deployment) ~ 0, 
    TRUE ~ deployment),
    alba_member = case_when(
      str_detect(statenme, "Venezuela") & year >= 2004 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "Cuba") & year >= 2004 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "Nicaragua") & year >= 2007 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "Bolivia") & year >= 2006 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "Ecuador") & year >= 2007 & year <= 2018 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "Honduras") & year >= 2008 & year <= 2009 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "Dominica") & year >= 2008 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "Antigua") & year >= 2009 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "St. Vincent") & year >= 2009 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "St. Kitts") & year >= 2014 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "Grenada") & year >= 2014 ~ 1,
      str_detect(statenme, "St. Lucia") & year >= 2013 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    gdppc = gdp_constant/population_total) |>
  group_by(ccode) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(deployment_cumsum = cumsum(deployment),
                deployment_lead_1 = dplyr::lead(deployment, n = 1L),
                deployment_lead_2 = dplyr::lead(deployment, n = 2L)) |>
  group_by(ccode, deployment_cumsum) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(time_since_deployment = seq_along(deployment_cumsum) - 1) |>
  ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(across(c(exports_to_us, imports_from_us, v2x_polyarchy, gdp_constant, gdppc, infant_mortality_rate, population_total, population_urban, education_spending, healthcare_expenditures, population_rural, un_distance, USAgree, unemployment_rate, time_since_deployment, homicide_rate), 
                       ~arm::rescale(.x),
                       .names = "{.col}_z"),
                across(c(exports_to_us, imports_from_us, gdppc, gdp_constant, population_total, infant_mortality_rate),
                       ~log(.x),
                       .names = "log_{.col}")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(c(iraq_coalition, dead, wounded, troopstotal, troopspeak),
                       ~ case_when(
                         is.na(.x) ~ 0,
                         TRUE ~ .x
                       ))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(iraq_coalition_general = case_when(
    ccode %in% iraq.ccode.list ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  )) |> 
  dplyr::filter(ccode != 70) |> 
  dplyr::select(!contains("country.")) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(row_index = row_number())



# Generate limited nested dataset for comparison

data.analysis.nested <- data.analysis |> 
  drop_na(deployment_lead_1, deployment_lead_2, log_gdppc, log_imports_from_us, log_population_total, population_urban, v2x_polyarchy, un_distance, alba_member, iraq_coalition, log_infant_mortality_rate, homicide_rate, education_spending, time_since_deployment) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(row_index = row_number())
  

# Write data file for main data
readr::write_csv(data.analysis,
                 here::here("Data/data-analysis.csv"))


# Write data file for nested data
readr::write_csv(data.analysis.nested,
                 here::here("Data/data-analysis-nested.csv"))

}

```

# Analysis


## Create Map of Deployment Locations

```{r deployment-map}

deploy.count <- data.analysis |>
  dplyr::select(statenme, year, deployment) |> 
  filter(year >= 1998) |> 
  dplyr::rename("Country" = "statenme", "Year" = "year") |> 
  group_by(Country) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Count = sum(deployment, na.rm = TRUE)) 


mapdata <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") |> 
  dplyr::filter(region_wb == "Latin America & Caribbean") |> 
  dplyr::left_join(deploy.count, by = c("name" = "Country")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Count = ifelse(is.na(Count), 0, Count)) |> 
  dplyr::filter(sovereignt != "Mexico")

coastline <- rnaturalearth::ne_coastline(scale = "medium",
                                         returnclass = "sf")

mapplot <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = coastline,
          aes(geometry = geometry),
          linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = mapdata, 
          aes(fill = Count),
          color = "black", size = 0.1) +

  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option = "turbo",
                              begin = 0.05,
                              end = 1.0,
                              direction = 1) +
  flynnprojects::theme_flynn_map(base_size = 11, base_family = "oswald") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = rel(1.2))) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-100, -30),
           ylim = c(25.25, -57.3)) +
  theme(legend.title = element_text(margin = margin(b = 8))) +
  labs(title = "Humanitarian and Civic Assistance Deployment Locations, 1998-2025",
       fill = "Number of\nDeployments") 

ggsave(here::here("Figures/deployment_map.png"), 
       width = 6, 
       height = 4, 
       dpi = 400)

# Generate histogram with coloring.

histplot <- ggplot(deploy.count, aes(x = Count, group = Count, fill = Count)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1,
                 show.legend = FALSE,
                 linewidth = 0.1,
                 color = "black") +
  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option = "turbo",
                              begin = 0.05,
                              end = 1.0,
                              direction = 1) +
  flynnprojects::theme_flynn_map(base_size = 6, base_family = "oswald") + 
  theme(axis.text.x.bottom = element_text(),
        axis.title.x.bottom = element_text(size = rel(1.1),
                                           margin = margin(t = 0.2, unit = "cm"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,17,1)) +
  labs(x = "Count",
       y  = "",
       fill = "Count")


## Create table for top five recipients

tableplot <- gt::gt(deploy.count |> 
                                     arrange(-Count) |> 
                                     slice(1:5)) |> 
  gt::tab_header(title = "Top 5 Deployment Locations") |> 
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = 9,
                  heading.title.font.weight = "bold",
                  column_labels.font.weight = "bold")
  
  
  
## Combine all into single plot
com.1 <- mapplot + 
  inset_element(histplot,
                left = 0.79,
                right = 1.43,
                bottom = 0.20,
                top = 0.48,
                align_to = "full",
                on_top = FALSE) 

com.2 <- com.1 + 
  inset_element(tableplot,
                left = 0.92,
                right = 0.90,
                bottom = 0.60,
                top = 0.80,
                align_to = "full",
                on_top = FALSE) 

ggsave(here::here("Figures/deployment_map_full.png"), 
       width = 9,
       height = 5, 
       dpi = 400)


```


## Models


### Full Models

```{r brms-models-base-lead-1}
#| echo: false
#| message: false


ITERS <- 7000
CHAINS <- 4
WARMUP <- ITERS/2
CORES <- 4
THIN <- 1

PRIORS <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), class = "b"),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept")
)



model.econ.l1 <- brm(deployment_lead_1 ~ gdppc_z + imports_from_us_z + population_total_z + population_urban_z  ,
              data = data.analysis,
              prior = PRIORS,
              family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
              chains = CHAINS,
              iter = ITERS,
              warmup = WARMUP,
              cores = CORES,
              thin = THIN,
              backend = "cmdstanr",
              threads = threading(2),
              control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99,
                             max_treedepth = 13),
              save_model = here::here("Models/econ_model_lead_1.rds"),
              file_refit = "on_change")



model.political.l1 <- brm(deployment_lead_1 ~ v2x_polyarchy_z + un_distance_z + alba_member + iraq_coalition  ,
              data = data.analysis,
              prior = PRIORS,
              family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
              chains = CHAINS,
              iter = ITERS,
              warmup = WARMUP,
              cores = CORES,
              thin = THIN,
              backend = "cmdstanr",
              threads = threading(2),
              control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99,
                             max_treedepth = 13),
              save_model = here::here("Models/political_model_lead_1.rds"),
              file_refit = "on_change")



model.need.l1 <- brm(deployment_lead_1 ~ infant_mortality_rate_z + homicide_rate_z + education_spending_z + healthcare_expenditures_z  ,
              data = data.analysis,
              prior = PRIORS,
              family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
              chains = CHAINS,
              iter = ITERS,
              warmup = WARMUP,
              cores = CORES,
              thin = THIN,
              backend = "cmdstanr",
              threads = threading(2),
              control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99,
                             max_treedepth = 13),
              save_model = here::here("Models/need_model_lead_1.rds"),
              file_refit = "on_change")


model.combined.l1 <- brm(deployment_lead_1 ~ gdppc_z + imports_from_us_z + population_total_z + population_urban_z + v2x_polyarchy_z + un_distance_z + alba_member + iraq_coalition + infant_mortality_rate_z + homicide_rate_z + education_spending_z + healthcare_expenditures_z   ,
              data = data.analysis,
              prior = PRIORS,
              family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
              chains = CHAINS,
              iter = ITERS,
              warmup = WARMUP,
              cores = CORES,
              thin = THIN,
              backend = "cmdstanr",
              threads = threading(2),
              control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99,
                             max_treedepth = 13),
              save_model = here::here("Models/combined_model_lead_1.rds"),
              file_refit = "on_change")



# Set prior for full modeling containing varying intercepts for countries. 

PRIORS <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), class = "b"),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(gamma(1,1), class = "sd", group = "statenme"),
  prior(gamma(1,1), class = "sd", coef = "Intercept", group = "statenme"),
  prior(gamma(1,1), class = "sds", coef = "s(year)")
)

model.full.l1 <- brm(deployment_lead_1 ~ gdppc_z + imports_from_us_z + population_total_z + population_urban_z + v2x_polyarchy_z + un_distance_z + alba_member + iraq_coalition + infant_mortality_rate_z + homicide_rate_z + education_spending_z + healthcare_expenditures_z + s(year) + (1|statenme),
              data = data.analysis,
              prior = PRIORS,
              family = bernoulli(link = "logit"),
              chains = CHAINS,
              iter = ITERS,
              warmup = WARMUP,
              cores = CORES,
              thin = THIN,
              backend = "cmdstanr",
              threads = threading(2),
              control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99,
                             max_treedepth = 13),
              save_model = here::here("Models/full_model_lead_1.rds"),
              file_refit = "on_change")


```

#Tables


## Full Model 

```{r tables-full-model}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

# Set model list
mod.list <- list("Economic" = model.econ.l1, 
                 "Political" = model.political.l1, 
                 "Need" = model.need.l1,
                 "Combined" = model.combined.l1,
                 "Full" = model.full.l1)

# Set coefficient names 
coef.names <- c("b_gdppc_z" = "GDP Per Capita",
                "b_imports_from_us_z" = "Imports from US",
                "b_population_total_z" = "Total Population",
                "b_population_urban_z" = "Percent Urban Population",
                "b_v2x_polyarchy_z" = "Polyarchy Score",
                "b_un_distance_z" = "UN Voting Distance",
                "b_alba_member" = "ALBA Member",
                "b_iraq_coalition" = "Iraq Coalition Member",
                "b_infant_mortality_rate_z" = "Infant Mortality Rate",
                "b_unemployment_rate_z" = "Unemployment Rate",
                "b_healthcare_expenditures_z" = "Healthcare Expenditures",
                "b_education_spending_z" = "Education Spending")


# Set goodness of fit statistics
gof.names <- c("nobs",
               "ngroups",
               "nclusters",
               "elpd",
               "waic",
               "looic"
               )

# Set group index
group.index <- as.data.frame(coef.names) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(group = c("Economic", "Economic", "Economic", "Economic", 
                          "Political", "Political", "Political", "Political", 
                          "Need", "Need", "Need", "Need")
                ) |> 
  rownames_to_column(var = "raw") |> 
  dplyr::rename("clean" = "coef.names") 



tab <- modelsummary(mod.list,
             estimate = "{estimate} [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
             coef_map = coef.names,
             gof_map = gof.names,
             booktabs = TRUE,
             title = "Bayesian logistic models predicting deployments \\label{tab:cymodels}") 


tab.formatted <- tab |> 
  tinytable::group_tt(i = list(
    "Economic" = 1,
    "Political" = 5,
    "Need" = 9,
    "Model Fit" = 13
  )) |> 
  tinytable::theme_tt("bootstrap") |>
  tinytable::theme_tt("resize", width = 0.9) |> 
  tinytable::style_tt(i = c(1,6,11,16),
                      background = "gray") |> 
  tinytable::style_tt(i = 15,
                      line = "b",
                      line_width = 0.2,
                      line_color = "black") |> 
  tinytable::save_tt(here::here("Tables/model_summary.tex"),
                     overwrite = TRUE)


```

# Figures

## Coefficient Plots

```{r coefficient-plots-base}


# Coefficient plots for the base models

set.seed(66502)

mod.list <- list(model.econ.l2,
                 model.political.l2,
                 model.need.l2,
                 model.combined.l2,
                 model.full.l2)

mod.names <- c("Economic", "Political", "Need", "Combined", "Full")

names(mod.list) <- mod.names

coef.plot <- purrr::map2(.x = seq_along(mod.list),
                         .y = seq_along(mod.names),
                        .f = ~brms::as_draws_df(mod.list[[.x]],
                                             variable = "b_",
                                             regex = TRUE) |> 
                          dplyr::slice_sample(n = 100) |> 
                          dplyr::select(-b_Intercept) |> 
                          tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = everything()) |> 
                          dplyr::mutate(`Model Group` = mod.names[[.y]],
                                        name.full = case_when(
                                          grepl(".*poly.*", name) ~ "Polyarchy Score",
                                          grepl(".*dist.*", name) ~ "UN Distance",
                                          grepl(".*iraq*", name) ~ "Iraq Coalition",
                                          grepl(".*alba.*", name) ~ "ALBA Member",
                                          grepl(".*infant.*", name) ~ "Infant Mortality Rate",
                                          grepl(".*homicide.*", name) ~ "Homicide Rate",
                                          grepl(".*educ.*", name) ~ "Education Spending",
                                          grepl(".*health.*", name) ~ "Healthcare Spending",
                                          grepl(".*import.*", name) ~ "Imports from US",
                                          grepl(".*_total.*", name) ~ "Population (Total)",
                                          grepl(".*_urban.*", name) ~ "Population (Urban)",
                                          grepl(".*gdppc.*", name) ~ "GDP Per Capita"
                                        )
                                        )
                        )

coef.plot.df <- data.table::rbindlist(coef.plot) |> 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(name.full)) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(name.full = factor(name.full,
                                   levels = c("GDP Per Capita", "Imports from US", "Population (Total)", "Population (Urban)",
                                              "Polyarchy Score", "UN Distance", "Iraq Coalition", "ALBA Member",
                                              "Infant Mortality Rate", "Education Spending", "Healthcare Spending", "Homicide Rate"))) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(`Model Group` = factor(`Model Group`,
                                       levels = c("Full", "Combined", "Need", "Political", "Economic")))


ggplot(coef.plot.df, aes(y = reorder(name.full, -as.numeric(name.full)), x = value, color = `Model Group`, fill = `Model Group`)) +
  ggdist::stat_slabinterval(.width = c(0.5, 0.89),
                            position = "dodge",
                            color = "black",
                            slab_alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  facet_grid(name.full ~ .,
             scales = "free",
             switch="both") +
  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option = "magma",
                              discrete = TRUE,
                              begin = 0.2,
                              end = 0.9) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE),
         fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  theme_flynn(base_size = 11, base_family = "oswald") +
  theme(strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = 8, angle = 0, hjust = 0),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y.left = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = "Estimate",
       y = "Coefficient")

ggsave(here::here("Figures/coefficient-plot.png"),
       width = 7.5,
       height = 8.5,
       unit = "in")


```

## Separation Plots

```{r separation-plots-base}

# Set model list
mod.list <- list("Economic" = model.econ.l1, 
                 "Political" = model.political.l1, 
                 "Need" = model.need.l1,
                 "Combined" = model.combined.l1,
                 "Full" = model.full.l1)

# Generate 500 posterior draws of the expected value (i.e. 0 or 1)
# The posterior_predict function generates a matrix with columns representing individual cases rather than rows. 
# Need to convert columns to rows using the t() function.
# Use map() function to run over all of the models in mod.list (see above)

posterior.list <- map(.x = seq_along(mod.list), 
                      .f = ~ t(brms::posterior_epred(mod.list[[.x]], 
                                                     ndraws = 500,
                                                     re_formula = NULL)) |> 
                       as.data.frame() |> 
                       rowwise() |> 
                       dplyr::mutate(posterior_mean = mean(c_across(everything()))) |> 
                       bind_cols(mod.list[[.x]]$data) |> 
                        dplyr::mutate(predicted_deployment = case_when(posterior_mean > 0.08 ~ 1, 
                                                                       TRUE ~ 0)
                                      ) 
                      )
                      
# Combine the separate list elements into a single data frame. 
# Use the idcol argument to identify the separate models from the list elements.
sep.plot.data <- data.table::rbindlist(posterior.list, idcol = TRUE, fill = TRUE) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(.id = case_when(.id == 1 ~ "Economic",
                               .id == 2 ~ "Political",
                               .id == 3 ~ "Need",
                               .id == 4 ~ "Combined",
                               .id == 5 ~ "Full"),
                .id = factor(.id, 
                             levels = c("Economic", "Political", "Need", "Combined", "Full"))) |> 
  group_by(.id) |>
  arrange(posterior_mean) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(index = row_number()) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c("V1":"V500"))



# Plot the separation plot
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = sep.plot.data |> filter(deployment_lead_1 == 0), aes(x = index, xmin = index-0.5, xmax = index+0.5, y = posterior_mean, ymin=0, ymax = 1), fill = "gray95", show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 1, ) +
    geom_rect(data = sep.plot.data |> filter(deployment_lead_1 == 1), aes(x = index, xmin = index-0.5, xmax = index+0.5, y = posterior_mean, ymin=0, ymax = 1), fill = "black", show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 1, ) +
  stat_lineribbon(data = sep.plot.data, aes(x = index, y = value), .width = ppoints(50), show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.6) +
  #geom_line(data = sep.plot.data, aes(x = index, y = posterior_mean), color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(. ~ .id,
             scales = "free_x",
             ncol = 1) +
  theme_flynn(base_family = "oswald", base_size = 10) +
  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option = "plasma",
                              begin = 0,
                              end = 1.0,
                              discrete = TRUE,
                              direction = -1)  +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 10),
```

## ROC Curve Plots

```{r roc-curves-base}

# Set model list
mod.list <- list("Economic" = model.econ.l1, 
                 "Political" = model.political.l1, 
                 "Need" = model.need.l1,
                 "Combined" = model.combined.l1,
                 "Full" = model.combined.l1)

# Generate 100 posterior draws of the expected value (i.e. 0 or 1)
# The posterior_epred function generates a matrix with columns representing individual cases rather than rows. 
# Need to convert columns to rows using the t() function.
# Use map() function to run over all of the models in mod.list (see above)

posterior.list <- map(.x = seq_along(mod.list), 
                       .f = ~ t(brms::posterior_epred(mod.list[[.x]], 
                                                      ndraws = 100,
                                                      re_fomula = NULL)) |> 
                         as.data.frame() |> 
                         rowwise() |> 
                         dplyr::mutate(posterior_mean = mean(c_across(everything()))) |> 
                         bind_cols(mod.list[[.x]]$data) |> 
                        mutate(probs = list(seq(0.01, 1.0, 0.01)))
                      )

roc.df <- data.table::rbindlist(posterior.list, 
                                idcol = TRUE, 
                                fill = TRUE) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(.id = case_when(.id == 1 ~ "Economic",
                               .id == 2 ~ "Political",
                               .id == 3 ~ "Need",
                               .id == 4 ~ "Combined",
                               .id == 5 ~ "Full"),
                .id = factor(.id, 
                             levels = c("Full", "Combined", "Need", "Political", "Economic"))) |> 
  group_by(.id) |>
  arrange(posterior_mean) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(index = row_number()) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c("V1":"V100")) |> 
  unnest(probs) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(predicted_deployment = case_when(value > probs ~ 1, 
                                                 TRUE ~ 0),
                true_positive = case_when(deployment_lead_1 == 1 & predicted_deployment == 1 ~ 1,
                                          TRUE ~ 0),
                false_positive = case_when(deployment_lead_1 == 0 & predicted_deployment == 1 ~ 1,
                                           TRUE ~ 0),
                true_negative = case_when(deployment_lead_1 == 0 & predicted_deployment == 0 ~ 1,
                                          TRUE ~ 0),
                false_negative = case_when(deployment_lead_1 == 1 & predicted_deployment == 0 ~ 1,
                                           TRUE ~ 0)) |> 
  group_by(.id, probs) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sensitivity = sum(true_positive)/(sum(true_positive) + sum(false_negative)),
                specificity = sum(true_negative)/(sum(true_negative) + sum(false_positive)),
                precision = sum(true_positive)/(sum(true_positive) + sum(false_positive)),
                recall = sum(true_positive)/(sum(true_positive) + sum(false_negative))) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(sensitivity = mean(sensitivity),
                   specificity = mean(specificity),
                   precision = mean(precision),
                   recall = mean(recall))


ggplot(roc.df, aes(x = 1 - specificity, y = sensitivity, color = .id, linetype = .id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_flynn(base_family = "oswald", base_size = 10) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
  labs(x = "False Positive Rate",
       y = "True Positive Rate",
       title = "ROC Curves for Base Models") +
  viridis::scale_color_viridis(option = "turbo",
                               discrete = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), limits = c(0,1.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0), limits = c(0,1.01)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(margin = margin(r = 0.2, unit = "cm"))) +
  labs(color = "Model",
       linetype = "Model")

ggsave(here::here("Figures/roc_curves_base.png"), width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 400)

```

```{r book-code-test}

model.econ$data$predicted <- as.data.frame(predict(model.econ))
model.political$data$predicted <- as.data.frame(predict(model.political))
model.need$data$predicted <- as.data.frame(predict(model.need))
model.combined$data$predicted <- as.data.frame(predict(model.combined))


op.predict.list <- list(model.econ$data, 
                        model.political$data, 
                        model.need$data, 
                        model.combined$data)

# Create loop to generate ROC curve for different p values
results <- list()

prob <-  1

for(prob in 1:1000) {
# Huzzah!
  
op.predict.list.2 <- lapply(op.predict.list, function(x) 
  dplyr::select(x, predicted, deployment_lead_1) %>% 
    mutate(predicted.value = ifelse(predicted$Estimate >= (prob/1000), 1, 0),
           match = ifelse(deployment_lead_1 == 1 & predicted.value == 1 | deployment_lead_1 == 0 & predicted.value == 0, 1, 0),
           percent.correct = sum(match)/length(match),
           false.neg = ifelse(predicted.value == 0 & deployment_lead_1 == 1, 1, 0),
           false.pos = ifelse(predicted.value == 1 & deployment_lead_1 == 0, 1, 0),
           true.neg = ifelse(deployment_lead_1 == 0 & predicted.value == 0, 1, 0),
           true.pos = ifelse(deployment_lead_1 == 1 & predicted.value == 1, 1, 0),
           total.no = ifelse(deployment_lead_1 == 0, 1, 0),
           total.yes = ifelse(deployment_lead_1 == 1, 1, 0)) %>% 
    dplyr::summarise(percent.correct = mean(percent.correct),
                     false.neg = sum(false.neg),
                     false.pos = sum(false.pos),
                     true.neg = sum(true.neg),
                     true.pos = sum(true.pos),
                     total.no = sum(total.no),
                     total.yes = sum(total.yes)) %>% 
    mutate(`False Positive Rate` = false.pos/total.no,
           `False Negative Rate` = false.neg/total.yes,
           `Sensitivity` = true.pos/total.yes,
           `Specificity` = true.neg/total.no,
           pvalue = prob/1000))

op.predict.df <- bind_rows(op.predict.list.2) %>% 
  mutate(Model = c("Economic", "Political", "Need", "Combined")) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Model, percent.correct, `False Positive Rate`, `False Negative Rate`, `Sensitivity`, `Specificity`, pvalue) 

results[[prob]] <- op.predict.df

prob <- prob + 1 
}

results.df <- bind_rows(results) %>% 
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = c("Economic", "Political", "Need", "Combined")))
```

## Country Varying Intercepts

```{r country-varying-intercepts-combined}

library(brms)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidybayes)
library(patchwork)

# Extract 500 posterior samples for country varying intercepts from each model
set.seed(123)

# Function to extract and prepare random effects
extract_country_intercepts <- function(model, model_name, n_samples = 500) {
  # Extract random effects for countries
  country_samples <- model %>%
    spread_draws(r_statenme[statenme, ], ndraws = n_samples) %>%
    rename(intercept = r_statenme) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
  
  return(country_samples)
}

# Extract from all four models
econ_intercepts <- extract_country_intercepts(model.econ, "Economic")
political_intercepts <- extract_country_intercepts(model.political, "Political")
need_intercepts <- extract_country_intercepts(model.need, "Need")
combined_intercepts <- extract_country_intercepts(model.combined, "Combined")


# Extract from all four models
econ_intercepts_nested <- extract_country_intercepts(model.econ.nested, "Economic Nested")
political_intercepts_nested <- extract_country_intercepts(model.political.nested, "Political Nested")
need_intercepts_nested <- extract_country_intercepts(model.need.nested, "Need Nested")
combined_intercepts_nested <- extract_country_intercepts(model.combined.nested, "Combined Nested")


# Combine all samples
all_intercepts <- bind_rows(
  econ_intercepts,
  political_intercepts,
  need_intercepts,
  combined_intercepts,
  econ_intercepts_nested,
  political_intercepts_nested,
  need_intercepts_nested,
  combined_intercepts_nested
) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(statenme = gsub("\\.", " ", statenme),
                nesting_group = case_when(
                  grepl(".*Nested.*", model) ~ "Nested",
                  TRUE ~ "Base"
                ),
                model = gsub(" Nested", "", model),
                model = factor(model,
                               levels = c("Combined", "Need", "Economic", "Political")))

# Create caterpillar plot with all models
plot_all_models <- all_intercepts %>%
  group_by(nesting_group, statenme, model) %>%
  median_qi(intercept, .width = c(0.5, 0.95)) %>%
  group_by(statenme) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(intercept_avg = mean(intercept[nesting_group == "Base"])) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = reorder(statenme, intercept_avg), 
             x = intercept, 
             color = model, 
             shape = model)) +
  geom_pointinterval(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
                     aes(xmin = .lower, xmax = .upper)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, 
             linetype = "dashed", 
             alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(. ~ nesting_group,
             scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title = "Country-Specific Intercepts Across Models",
    subtitle = "Points show medians and bands correspond to 50% and 95% credible intervals",
    x = "Country-Specific Intercept (Log-Odds)",
    y = "Country",
    color = "Model",
    shape = "Model"
  ) +
  viridis::scale_color_viridis(option = "magma",
                              discrete = TRUE,
                              begin = 0.2,
                              end = 0.9) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE),
         shape = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  theme_flynn(base_family = "oswald", base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)
  )

print(plot_all_models)

ggsave(here::here("Figures/figure-intercept-plot-combined.png"),
       dpi = 400,
       height = 9,
       width = 7)



```



# Variance Analysis

```{r}
library(brms)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidybayes)
library(bayesplot)
library(ggdist)
library(patchwork)
library(corrplot)

# ============================================================================
# 1. EXTRACT VARYING INTERCEPTS FROM ALL MODELS
# ============================================================================

# Function to extract country intercepts with model name
extract_country_intercepts <- function(model, model_name) {
  # Get summary statistics
  intercepts_summary <- ranef(model)$statenme[, , "Intercept"] %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("statenme") %>%
    rename(
      estimate = Estimate,
      est_error = Est.Error,
      lower_95 = Q2.5,
      upper_95 = Q97.5
    ) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
  
  # Get posterior draws
  intercepts_draws <- model %>%
    spread_draws(r_statenme[statenme, ], ndraws = 1000) %>%
    rename(intercept = r_statenme) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
  
  return(list(summary = intercepts_summary, draws = intercepts_draws))
}

# Extract from all models
econ_results <- extract_country_intercepts(model.econ, "Economic")
political_results <- extract_country_intercepts(model.political, "Political")
need_results <- extract_country_intercepts(model.need, "Need")
combined_results <- extract_country_intercepts(model.combined, "Combined")

# Combine summaries and draws
all_summaries <- bind_rows(
  econ_results$summary,
  political_results$summary,
  need_results$summary,
  combined_results$summary
)

all_draws <- bind_rows(
  econ_results$draws,
  political_results$draws,
  need_results$draws,
  combined_results$draws
)

# ============================================================================
# 2. CORRELATION MATRIX BETWEEN MODELS
# ============================================================================

# Create wide format for correlation analysis
intercepts_wide <- all_summaries %>%
  select(statenme, model, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = estimate)

# Calculate correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- intercepts_wide %>%
  select(-statenme) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

print("Correlation Matrix of Country Intercepts Across Models:")
print(round(cor_matrix, 3))

# Visualize correlation matrix
corrplot(cor_matrix, 
         method = "color", 
         type = "upper",
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.srt = 45,
         addCoef.col = "black",
         title = "Correlations of Country Intercepts Between Models",
         mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0),
         col = colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(200))

# ============================================================================
# 3. PAIRWISE SCATTERPLOTS
# ============================================================================

library(GGally)

plot_pairs <- intercepts_wide %>%
  select(-statenme) %>%
  ggpairs(
    title = "Pairwise Relationships of Country Intercepts Across Models",
    upper = list(continuous = wrap("cor", size = 5, color = "darkblue")),
    lower = list(continuous = wrap("points", alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5)),
    diag = list(continuous = wrap("densityDiag", fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5))
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(plot_pairs)

# Individual scatterplots with country labels
plot_econ_political <- ggplot(intercepts_wide, 
                               aes(x = Economic, y = Political)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkblue", fill = "lightblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = statenme), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 10) +
  labs(
    title = "Economic vs Political Model Intercepts",
    x = "Economic Model Intercept",
    y = "Political Model Intercept"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot_econ_need <- ggplot(intercepts_wide, 
                         aes(x = Economic, y = Need)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 3, color = "coral") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkred", fill = "lightcoral") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = statenme), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 10) +
  labs(
    title = "Economic vs Need Model Intercepts",
    x = "Economic Model Intercept",
    y = "Need Model Intercept"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot_combined_econ <- ggplot(intercepts_wide, 
                              aes(x = Combined, y = Economic)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 3, color = "forestgreen") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkgreen", fill = "lightgreen") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = statenme), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = 10) +
  labs(
    title = "Combined vs Economic Model Intercepts",
    subtitle = "Dotted line shows perfect agreement",
    x = "Combined Model Intercept",
    y = "Economic Model Intercept"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Combine plots
(plot_econ_political | plot_econ_need) / plot_combined_econ

# ============================================================================
# 4. IDENTIFY COUNTRIES WITH DIVERGENT INTERCEPTS ACROSS MODELS
# ============================================================================

# Calculate variance across models for each country
intercept_variance <- intercepts_wide %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    mean_intercept = mean(c(Economic, Political, Need, Combined), na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_intercept = sd(c(Economic, Political, Need, Combined), na.rm = TRUE),
    range_intercept = max(c(Economic, Political, Need, Combined), na.rm = TRUE) - 
                      min(c(Economic, Political, Need, Combined), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(sd_intercept))

# Top 10 countries with most variation across models
print("Countries with highest variation across models:")
print(intercept_variance %>% 
        select(statenme, mean_intercept, sd_intercept, range_intercept) %>%
        head(10))

# Visualize variation
plot_variation <- intercept_variance %>%
  slice_max(sd_intercept, n = 15) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Economic, Political, Need, Combined),
               names_to = "model", values_to = "intercept") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = intercept, group = statenme)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = model), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~reorder(statenme, -sd_intercept), ncol = 5) +
  labs(
    title = "Countries with Most Variation Across Models",
    subtitle = "Top 15 countries by standard deviation of intercepts",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Country Intercept"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

print(plot_variation)

# ============================================================================
# 5. HEATMAP OF COUNTRY INTERCEPTS ACROSS MODELS
# ============================================================================

# Prepare data for heatmap
heatmap_data <- all_summaries %>%
  select(statenme, model, estimate)

plot_heatmap <- ggplot(heatmap_data, 
                       aes(x = model, y = reorder(statenme, estimate), 
                           fill = estimate)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC", 
    mid = "white", 
    high = "#B2182B",
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Intercept"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Country-Specific Intercepts Across All Models",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

print(plot_heatmap)

# ============================================================================
# 6. POSTERIOR UNCERTAINTY COMPARISON
# ============================================================================

# Compare uncertainty (credible interval width) across models
uncertainty_comparison <- all_summaries %>%
  mutate(ci_width = upper_95 - lower_95) %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_ci_width = mean(ci_width),
    median_ci_width = median(ci_width),
    sd_ci_width = sd(ci_width)
  )

print("Average uncertainty (95% CI width) by model:")
print(uncertainty_comparison)

# Visualize uncertainty by model
plot_uncertainty <- all_summaries %>%
  mutate(ci_width = upper_95 - lower_95) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = ci_width, fill = model)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.8, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Posterior Uncertainty in Country Intercepts by Model",
    subtitle = "Width of 95% credible intervals",
    x = "Model",
    y = "95% CI Width"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

print(plot_uncertainty)

# ============================================================================
# 7. SHRINKAGE COMPARISON ACROSS MODELS
# ============================================================================

# Compare how much countries are pulled toward the mean in each model
shrinkage_data <- intercepts_wide %>%
  mutate(
    abs_econ = abs(Economic),
    abs_political = abs(Political),
    abs_need = abs(Need),
    abs_combined = abs(Combined),
    mean_abs = (abs_econ + abs_political + abs_need + abs_combined) / 4
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abs))

# Countries with largest absolute intercepts
print("Countries with largest average absolute intercepts:")
print(shrinkage_data %>% 
        select(statenme, Economic, Political, Need, Combined, mean_abs) %>%
        head(10))

plot_shrinkage <- shrinkage_data %>%
  slice_max(mean_abs, n = 20) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Economic, Political, Need, Combined),
               names_to = "model", values_to = "intercept") %>%
  mutate(country_num = as.numeric(factor(reorder(statenme, mean_abs)))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = country_num, x = intercept, color = model)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(unique(shrinkage_data %>% 
                               slice_max(mean_abs, n = 20) %>% 
                               pull(statenme))),
    labels = shrinkage_data %>% 
      slice_max(mean_abs, n = 20) %>% 
      arrange(desc(mean_abs)) %>% 
      pull(statenme)
  ) +
  viridis::scale_color_viridis(option = "magma", discrete = TRUE, 
                               begin = 0.2, end = 0.9) +
  labs(
    title = "Countries with Largest Intercepts Across Models",
    subtitle = "Top 20 by average absolute intercept",
    x = "Country Intercept",
    y = "Country",
    color = "Model"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)
  )

print(plot_shrinkage)

# ============================================================================
# 8. CLASSIFICATION OF COUNTRIES BY MODEL AGREEMENT
# ============================================================================

# Classify countries by sign consistency across models
country_classification <- intercepts_wide %>%
  mutate(
    all_positive = Economic > 0 & Political > 0 & Need > 0 & Combined > 0,
    all_negative = Economic < 0 & Political < 0 & Need < 0 & Combined < 0,
    mixed = !all_positive & !all_negative,
    classification = case_when(
      all_positive ~ "Consistently High",
      all_negative ~ "Consistently Low",
      TRUE ~ "Mixed"
    )
  )

# Summary by classification
table(country_classification$classification)

# Visualize classification
plot_classification <- country_classification %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Economic, Political, Need, Combined),
               names_to = "model", values_to = "intercept") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = intercept, group = statenme, 
             color = classification)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~classification) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Consistently High" = "#B2182B",
                                 "Consistently Low" = "#2166AC",
                                 "Mixed" = "#FDB863")) +
  labs(
    title = "Country Classifications by Intercept Consistency",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Country Intercept",
    color = "Classification"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(plot_classification)

# Print countries in each category
print("\nConsistently High countries:")
print(country_classification %>% 
        filter(all_positive) %>% 
        arrange(desc(Combined)) %>% 
        select(statenme, Economic, Political, Need, Combined))

print("\nConsistently Low countries:")
print(country_classification %>% 
        filter(all_negative) %>% 
        arrange(Combined) %>% 
        select(statenme, Economic, Political, Need, Combined))

# ============================================================================
# 9. STATISTICAL TESTS OF CORRELATION SIGNIFICANCE
# ============================================================================

# Test correlations using posterior draws
correlation_tests <- list()

model_pairs <- list(
  c("Economic", "Political"),
  c("Economic", "Need"),
  c("Economic", "Combined"),
  c("Political", "Need"),
  c("Political", "Combined"),
  c("Need", "Combined")
)

for (pair in model_pairs) {
  model1_draws <- all_draws %>% filter(model == pair[1])
  model2_draws <- all_draws %>% filter(model == pair[2])
  
  # Calculate correlation for each posterior draw
  cors <- model1_draws %>%
    inner_join(model2_draws, by = c("statenme", ".draw"), 
               suffix = c("_1", "_2")) %>%
    group_by(.draw) %>%
    summarise(correlation = cor(intercept_1, intercept_2))
  
  correlation_tests[[paste(pair[1], "vs", pair[2])]] <- cors %>%
    summarise(
      mean_cor = mean(correlation),
      median_cor = median(correlation),
      lower_95 = quantile(correlation, 0.025),
      upper_95 = quantile(correlation, 0.975),
      prob_positive = mean(correlation > 0),
      prob_high = mean(correlation > 0.7)
    )
}

correlation_test_results <- bind_rows(correlation_tests, .id = "comparison")

print("\nPosterior distributions of correlations between models:")
print(correlation_test_results)

# ============================================================================
# 10. SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

summary_stats <- all_summaries %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    n_countries = n(),
    mean_intercept = mean(estimate),
    sd_intercept = sd(estimate),
    min_intercept = min(estimate),
    max_intercept = max(estimate),
    range = max_intercept - min_intercept,
    n_positive = sum(estimate > 0),
    n_negative = sum(estimate < 0),
    prop_positive = n_positive / n_countries
  )

print("\nSummary statistics by model:")
print(summary_stats)
```

```{r misc-code}
# Posterior Predicted Average

                           allow_new_levels = TRUE)

# Posterior average for individual coefficients
test.2 <- brms::posterior_average(model.1, model.2,
                                  ndraws = 1e4, 
                                  weights = "waic")





marginaleffects::plot_slopes(model.combined,
                             variables = "infant_mortality_rate_z",
                             condition = "imports_from_us_z") 
  

test.slopes <- slopes(model.combined,
                      variables = c("infant_mortality_rate_z"),
                      condition = c("imports_from_us_z"),
                      conf_level = 0.95,
                      #type = "response",
                      newdata = datagrid(
                        imports_from_us_z = seq(2, 10, length.out = 20),
                        infant_mortality_rate_z = c(30))) |>
  posterior_draws()

mean.slopes <- test.slopes |> 
  dplyr::group_by(imports_from_us_z) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(mean_draw = mean(draw)) |> 
  dplyr::ungroup() |> 
  dplyr::mutate(imports_from_us_z = round(imports_from_us_z, 2))

# Spaghetti plot
ggplot() +
 geom_line(data = test.slopes, aes(x = imports_from_us_z, y = draw, group = drawid), alpha = 0.1, color = "dodgerblue") +
 stat_summary(data = test.slopes, aes(x = imports_from_us_z, y = draw), fun = mean, geom = "line", color = "black", size = 1.5) 

# Lineribbon plot
ggplot(test.slopes, aes(x = imports_from_us_z, y = draw)) +
  ggdist::stat_lineribbon(.width = c(0.5, 0.89, 0.95), alpha = 0.5) +
```
